pr_body:
Fixes #23345 A 304 response is supposed to have the same headers as its associated 200 response, including Cache-Control, but the 304 response itself should not be cached. Otherwise Http.Sys will serve the 304 response to all requests without checking conditional headers like If-None-Match.

@ricmrodrigues

issue_context.title: HTTP 304 response when using Http.sys for a request that should return a 200
issue_context.body:

### Describe the bug
Basically when requesting static files from a ASP.NET Core 3.1 web app without the appropriate request headers (If-None-Match for eg), I get an HTTP 304, incorrectly. This can come into a client that never had the file in the first place, causing a failure to load.

### To Reproduce

1) run the app locally but using httpsys as the web server
2) make a call to a static file that returns an ETag and a 200
3) make a subsequent call to the same with the ETag on the If-None-Match and get a 304
4) stop sending the ETag and verify you're still getting 304s

request looks like
```
GET https://.../vendor.5b4c15ae6ced0e36f7d3.js HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: PostmanRuntime/7.25.0
Accept: */*
Host: ...
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br
```

and response looks like
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000
Content-Type: application/javascript
Last-Modified: Wed, 24 Jun 2020 16:55:03 GMT
Accept-Ranges: bytes
ETag: "1d64a48345b98c8"
Server: *** Microsoft-HTTPAPI/2.0
Request-Context: appId=cid-v1:49d13409-b199-43ea-a259-e4893160bf92
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors https: http: ; script-src 'self' ...
X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: master-only;
Referrer-Policy: same-origin
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2020 21:34:26 GMT
```
### Exceptions (if any)
<!-- 
Include the exception you get when facing this issue
-->

### Further technical details
- ASP.NET Core version: 3.1
comments: Theory: Static Files produces the first 304 response (correctly), and http.sys caches this. On the next request http.sys serves the 304 from cache based only on the URL, it doesn't check the if-modified headers. Does the http.sys cache even implement conditional headers? If not we should prevent it from caching 304s.

review_comments: So HTTP.Sys doesn't use the If-None-Match header as part of the cache lookup key. Can that be configured somehow?
Why does this test do this, but not the following test?
There's no way to clear the cache between tests, this helps avoid collisions. Not sure why only half the tests have them, I'll add them to the other half.
